title: Rollback dashboard + safe-apply gate metrics spec (tags, queries, alert thresholds)
content:
Context
This doc defines the metrics + tags required to power:
1) the Optimization Rollout Health Dashboard (Grafana)
2) safe-apply gating (latency/5xx/saturation + quant quality gates)
3) alerts used by on-call during staged apply + rollback

This spec is intended to be implementable by:
- Serving Runtime (emission + tagging)
- Control Plane (rollout controller annotations + gate evaluation)
- Observability pack (dashboards + alert rules)

Non-goals
- This is not a full SLO spec for customer-facing endpoints.
- This is not a complete metrics taxonomy for all inference runtime metrics.


A. Required tags (labels) and cardinality rules
These labels MUST be present on all safe-apply/rollback gate metrics. If a metric cannot carry all labels (e.g., node-exporter), it cannot be used as a gate.

Required labels
- tenant_id: string
  - Hosted: Redwood tenant UUID
  - Dedicated: customer account UUID
  - Private: “tenant_id” should still be set (from private control plane); if unavailable, use “tenant_id=private:<cluster_id>” (temporary compatibility mode)
- model: canonical model name (e.g., “llama-3.1-70b-instruct”)
- region: serving region (e.g., “us-east-1”, “eu-west-1”, “onprem”) 
- config_version: immutable optimization config version id (e.g., “ocv_01J3…”) 

Required (rollout/gating) labels
- rollout_id: string identifier for a single staged apply attempt (e.g., “ocr_01J4…”). This is required for: rollout progression graphs, per-rollout alert scoping, and audit correlation.
- rollout_stage: enum {validate, canary, promote, rollback, steady}
- scope: enum {tenant, tenant_model, tenant_model_region}

Strongly recommended labels
- deployment_mode: enum {hosted, dedicated, private}
- worker_pool: runtime pool/shard identifier (low cardinality; e.g., “pool-a”, “pool-b”)
- quant_profile: string (only when quantization is enabled); do NOT attach quant_profile to every request metric in steady state unless specifically requested (cardinality)

Labels explicitly NOT allowed on gate metrics (cardinality/PII risk)
- request_id, trace_id, user_id, session_id
- prompt_hash, raw_prompt, tool_name
- full hostname / pod UID (ok for infra metrics but not gates)

Cardinality guardrails
- config_version + rollout_id is already a multiplicative label pair; do not add anything that grows with traffic volume.
- region should be the Redwood external region, not AZ.
- model should be canonical model id, not “model_instance_id”.


B. Metric definitions (names, types, semantics)
All metrics below are expected to be emitted to Prometheus (or compatible backend) and consumed by Grafana + slo-toolkit gate evaluator.

B1. Request/response health
1) redwood_inference_requests_total (counter)
- Labels: tenant_id, model, region, config_version, rollout_id, rollout_stage, deployment_mode, status_class
- status_class: {2xx, 4xx, 5xx}
- Notes: status_class is computed at the ingress/edge or runtime gateway. If emitting from runtime workers, ensure it reflects end-to-end request outcome.

2) redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket (histogram)
- Labels: tenant_id, model, region, config_version, rollout_id, rollout_stage, deployment_mode
- Semantics: end-to-end latency for inference call including queueing + compute, excluding client network. (We need consistency with existing dashboards; see observability-pack PR-20012.)

3) redwood_inference_queue_delay_seconds_bucket (histogram)
- Labels: same as above
- Semantics: time spent waiting in scheduler/queue before compute. This is a leading indicator for batching/caching regressions.

B2. Saturation / capacity signals (gateable)
4) redwood_runtime_gpu_utilization_ratio (gauge)
- Labels: tenant_id, model, region, config_version, rollout_id, rollout_stage, deployment_mode, worker_pool
- Semantics: 0..1 utilization (smoothed 30s). Use runtime’s internal view (not node exporter) so we can label by tenant/model scope.

5) redwood_runtime_kv_cache_hit_ratio (gauge)
- Labels: tenant_id, model, region, config_version, rollout_id, rollout_stage, deployment_mode
- Semantics: KV/prefix cache hit ratio (0..1). If caching disabled, emit 0 with cache_enabled=0 (optional label), or omit metric; for gates prefer explicit 0 + cache_enabled label to avoid silent missing.

6) redwood_runtime_batch_size (histogram)
- Labels: tenant_id, model, region, config_version, rollout_id, rollout_stage, deployment_mode
- Semantics: observed effective batch sizes. Used for debugging and “batching heuristics” rollouts.

7) redwood_runtime_oom_events_total (counter)
- Labels: tenant_id, model, region, config_version, rollout_id, rollout_stage, deployment_mode, worker_pool
- Semantics: runtime OOM or CUDA OOM events; gate should fail fast on any sustained OOMs.

B3. Quality signals (quantization gate)
These are only emitted when rollout_stage in {canary, promote} AND quantization is part of the config diff.

8) redwood_evals_canary_quality_score (gauge)
- Labels: tenant_id, model, region, config_version, rollout_id, rollout_stage, deployment_mode, eval_suite
- eval_suite: e.g., “prod_canary_v2”, “customer_<id>_smoke”
- Semantics: normalized 0..1 aggregate quality score from eval harness, with baseline-aligned scaling. (See Applied ML guidance; do not treat as an SLO.)

9) redwood_evals_canary_regression_p_value (gauge)
- Labels: same as above
- Semantics: p-value for regression test vs baseline version, if computed. Optional but recommended for noisy suites.


C. Gate evaluation: default thresholds + windows
Gate rules are implemented in slo-toolkit (PR-20023) and invoked by the rollout controller.

C1. Error-rate gate (mandatory)
Metric inputs
- Numerator: rate(redwood_inference_requests_total{status_class="5xx"}[5m])
- Denominator: rate(redwood_inference_requests_total[5m])

Default rule
- Fail if 5xx_rate > max(0.25%, baseline_5xx_rate + 0.15%) for 2 consecutive evaluations.
- Evaluation interval: 60s
- Lookback: 5m
- Minimum traffic for gate to be authoritative: denom >= 50 req/min (otherwise mark “insufficient traffic” and require manual operator confirmation to proceed).

Notes
- We use an absolute + relative threshold to avoid blocking low baseline tenants and to catch large regressions for high traffic tenants.
- For Dedicated/Private low-QPS tenants, gate can be overridden to a longer window (15m) and lower min traffic (10 req/min) with explicit approval.

C2. Latency gate p95 (mandatory)
Metric inputs
- p95 = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, tenant_id, model, region, config_version, rollout_id) (rate(redwood_inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])))

Default rule
- Fail if p95_latency_seconds > max(baseline_p95 * 1.15, baseline_p95 + 0.15s)
- AND fail fast if p95 increases by >30% within a single 2m window during canary.

Windows
- Primary: 5m lookback, eval every 60s
- Fast fail: 2m lookback, eval every 30s

Notes
- Baseline_p95 is computed from the immediately previous known-good config_version for the same (tenant_id, model, region). Control plane must provide baseline mapping.

C3. Latency gate p99 (recommended for large tenants)
Default rule
- Warn (do not auto-fail by default) if p99_latency_seconds > baseline_p99 * 1.20 for 5m.
- For top 20 tenants by traffic, we flip this to fail by default (SRE-managed allowlist).

C4. Queueing gate (recommended)
Default rule
- Fail if p95_queue_delay_seconds > max(baseline_queue_p95 * 1.25, baseline_queue_p95 + 0.10s) for 5m.

C5. OOM gate (mandatory)
Default rule
- Fail if increase(redwood_runtime_oom_events_total[5m]) > 0 AND traffic >= 10 req/min.
- This is a hard stop; canary should pause and require rollback decision.

C6. Saturation gate (soft)
Default rule
- Warn if gpu_utilization_ratio > 0.92 for 10m AND throughput does not increase.
- This is used as a “pause” signal, not an auto-fail, because utilization may rise under successful batching.

C7. Quantization quality gate (mandatory when quant is changed)
Inputs
- quality_score_delta = quality_score(candidate) - quality_score(baseline)

Default rule
- Fail if quality_score_delta < -0.02 sustained for 2 consecutive eval intervals (each eval interval corresponds to one canary eval run, typically ~3–7 minutes).
- Additionally fail if regression_p_value < 0.01 AND quality_score_delta < 0 (high confidence regression).

Notes
- Applied ML (Jonas/Arjun) requested small negative tolerance due to eval noise; thresholds may be suite-specific (eval_suite label).


D. Dashboard: required panels + annotations
Dashboard name
- “Optimization Rollout Health” (folder: Platform → Rollouts)

Time range defaults
- 6h (during incident), quick toggles 1h / 24h / 7d

Global filters (Grafana templating)
- tenant_id (required)
- model (required)
- region (optional, default: all)
- rollout_id (optional)
- config_version (optional)

Panels (minimum viable)
1) Rollout timeline
- Show current rollout_id, stage, canary %, start time, operator (from annotations).

2) 5xx rate (candidate vs baseline)
- Overlay series by config_version.

3) p95 latency (candidate vs baseline)
- Overlay; include vertical annotations at apply/promote/rollback.

4) p99 latency (optional by default)

5) Queue delay p95

6) Throughput (RPS) + token throughput (if available)
- If token throughput exists: redwood_inference_output_tokens_total (counter) labeled similarly.

7) GPU utilization (by worker_pool)

8) Cache hit ratio

9) OOM events
- Rate + last event time table.

10) Gate status summary (table)
- gate_name, pass/fail, last evaluated, reason, links to logs (rollout controller) and audit event id.

Annotations
- Emit Grafana annotations from control plane events stream:
  - optimization_config.apply_started
  - optimization_config.canary_progressed
  - optimization_config.promoted
  - optimization_config.rollback_started
  - optimization_config.rollback_completed
- Annotation fields: tenant_id, model, region, config_version_from, config_version_to, rollout_id, actor, change_reason


E. Alerting: rules and routing
Alert philosophy
- During active rollout (rollout_stage != steady), alerts should be tightly scoped to rollout_id and route to:
  - #eng-oncall + pager for Sev thresholds
  - #eng-platform for non-paging warnings
- Outside rollouts, these rules should not spam; rely on existing production SLO alerts.

E1. Paging alerts (during rollout)
1) RolloutGateFailed
- Trigger: any mandatory gate in {5xx, p95_latency, oom, quant_quality} fails
- Labels: tenant_id, model, region, rollout_id, config_version
- Paging: yes (Sev-2 default), escalates to Sev-1 if tenant in “enterprise_sla=true” list

2) RolloutStuck
- Trigger: rollout_stage=canary for > 30 minutes with no progression event
- Paging: no by default; warning to #eng-platform + #eng-sre

E2. Non-paging warnings (during rollout)
- p99 latency warn
- saturation warn
- queue delay warn

E3. Rollback verification alert (post-rollback)
RollbackDidNotRecover
- Trigger: rollback_completed event emitted AND within 10 minutes p95_latency is still > baseline_p95 * 1.10 OR 5xx_rate > baseline_5xx + 0.10%
- Paging: yes (because rollback is expected to be mitigation)

Routing
- Primary: SRE on-call
- Secondary: Platform Control Plane on-call
- FYI: Serving Runtime on-call if OOM/saturation


F. Implementation notes / open questions
1) Baseline computation
- Control plane needs a canonical “previous known-good config_version” pointer per scope.
- For partial canaries, baseline should be the currently active steady version for that same scope.

2) Missing metrics behavior
- Gate evaluator should treat missing metrics as “unknown” not “pass”.
- Exception: OOM gate can treat missing as pass only if runtime explicitly emits 0 series (preferred).

3) Partial rollout and mixed worker states
- If runtime reports mixed config_version within the same (tenant_id, model, region), show a “config skew” panel:
  - percent of requests served by each config_version.
- Metric: redwood_inference_requests_total already gives this if config_version label is correct.

4) Private deployments
- For Private, customers may not have our full dashboard pack. Provide a minimal JSON dashboard export + alert rules in installer.
- If tenant_id format differs, we need a compatibility mapping (see Required tags section).

5) Audit correlation
- Every rollout event should include audit_event_id; dashboard annotation should link to audit log entry.

Open questions (as of 2026-01-28)
- Do we need a “config_diff_risk_score” label/field surfaced in annotations to influence alert severity?
- For low-traffic tenants, should we require synthetic canary load to enable automated gates?
- Should saturation warnings block auto-promotion for Dedicated tiers by default?

Next steps
- Allison: align final metric names with runtime PR-19933 and ensure labels match (no drift)
- Aisha/Sean: finalize alert routing + paging policy for RollbackDidNotRecover
- Benji: ensure rollout controller emits rollout_id and stage onto gate evaluation metrics/events
- Chloe: confirm dashboard filter UX (tenant/model required) matches Console deep links
